chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

that he said — and he was at al-Hira during the era of Abu al-Abbas —: 'I went in to him while the people had doubts about the fast, and by Allah it was indeed from the month of Ramadan. I greeted him and he said: O Abu Abdillah, did you fast today? I said: No, and the meal was in front of him. He said: Come near and eat. He said: So I drew near and ate. He said: And I said: Fasting is with you and breaking fast is with you.'

Then the man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): You broke fast in a day from the month of Ramadan? He said: Yes, by Allah! Breaking a fast of a day from the month of Ramadan is more beloved to me than having my neck struck.

key_terms.أَبُو الْعَبَّاسِ: Abu al-Abbas — Abu al-Abbas al-Saffah, the first Abbasid caliph (r. 749–754 CE), known for his ruthlessness
key_terms.الصَّوْمُ: sawm (fasting) — the obligatory abstention from food, drink, and other things from dawn to sunset during Ramadan
key_terms.الْحِيرَةُ: al-Hira — a city in Iraq near Kufa, a seat of early Arab power, where the Imam was summoned or detained
key_terms.الْفِطْرُ: fitr (breaking the fast) — the act of eating or drinking that ends the fast
key_terms.تَقِيَّة: taqiyya (dissimulation) — concealing one's true beliefs or practices to protect oneself from harm

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about breaking the Ramadan fast under political duress?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts Imam al-Sadiq (AS) practicing taqiyya (religious dissimulation) during the Abbasid caliphate. While staying at al-Hira under the supervision of Abu al-Abbas al-Saffah (the first Abbasid caliph), the Imam broke his fast on a day he knew was from Ramadan, following the official calendar of the caliph which was in error. When questioned, the Imam declared emphatically that breaking the fast under such dangerous political circumstances was more precious to him than risking his life. This narrative illustrates the jurisprudential principle that taqiyya (dissimulation under duress) takes priority over outward religious observance when one's life is at risk.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, from Al Abbas Bin Aamir, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn, from a man from our companions,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said, and he<sup>asws</sup> was at Al-Hira during the era of Abu Al-Abbas (the governor): ‘And I<sup>asws</sup> went over to him, and the people had doubted regarding the Fast, and by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, it was from the Day of Ramazan. So I<sup>asws</sup> greeted to him. So he said, ‘O Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> have Fasted today?’ So I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’, and the meal was in front of him. He said, ‘So approach, and eat’. So I<sup>asws</sup> approached, and ate’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And I said, ‘The Fasting is with you, and the breaking is with you’.

So the man said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> broke Fast in a day from the Month of Ramazan?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Yes, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Breaking a Fast of a day from the Month of Ramazan is more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than if he were to strike off my<sup>asws</sup> neck’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ayyub ibn Nuh from al-‘ Abbas ibn ‘Amir from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from a man of our people who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘I, in the time of abu al- ‘Abbas, once was in al-Hirah, when I went before him and people had doubts about the fast, and that day, by Allah, was of the month of Ramadan. I said Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) to him and he asked, “O abu ‘Abd Allah, have you fasted today?” I replied, “No, I have not fasted;” the table was before him. He said, “Come close and eat.” He (the Imam) said, ‘I went close and ate, and said, “I fast with you and eat with you.’”

A man then said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Did you eat on the day of the month of Ramadan?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, by Allah, eating on one day of the month of Ramadan is more beloved to me than my neck being cut off.’”
